outlooks.summary: One or two organized clusters of thunderstorms are expected to evolve across parts of eastern Texas and southeastern Oklahoma through the lower Mississippi Valley and northwest Gulf coast region today into tonight. Activity will initially be accompanied by a risk for severe hail, before the risk for damaging wind gusts becomes more prominent. A few tornadoes are also possible.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Amplification within the westerlies emanating from the mid-latitude Pacific appears likely to continue to translate inland across the Pacific coast and the Rockies into the Plains during this period. Within this regime, large-scale ridging is in the process of building across the Pacific coast and U.S. intermountain region, and is forecast to expand across the Rockies into the Canadian prairies and northern U.S. Plains through tonight. Within the southern branch of splitting downstream flow, models indicate that upper trough amplification will proceed southeast of the central and southern Plains, toward the lower Mississippi Valley. This is expected to be accompanied by at least modest lower/mid tropospheric cyclogenesis, which may commence along a quasi-stationary frontal zone near the southern Plains Red River early today. East of the Red River Valley, the front has stalled across the Ozark Plateau and Tennessee Valley into the Mid Atlantic Coast region, and it appears that the primary frontal wave will track along this feature through the Ozark Plateau and adjacent portions of the Mississippi Valley by 12Z Thursday. sections.title: South central states
sections.text: Perhaps aided by forcing for ascent associated with an impulse emerging from troughing within the subtropical stream, over the Mexican Plateau, guidance remains suggestive that storms may initiate on the leading edge of the richer low-level moisture return near/inland of upper Texas and Louisiana coastal areas around or shortly after 12Z this morning. Although lower/mid tropospheric wind fields may be somewhat modest in strength (30-40+ kt) across this area, and in fact much of the warm sector through much of the period, given the anticipated destabilization, hodographs probably will be at least marginally conducive to supercells. Guidance suggests that is possible that forcing for ascent could contribute to the upscale growth of an evolving mesoscale convective system across at least southern Louisiana thereafter. The influence of convective outflow generated by this early activity on continued northward advection of the richer boundary layer moisture into the lower Mississippi Valley remains unclear. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of damaging winds, large hail, and a few tornadoes are expected today into this evening especially across parts of east Texas, southeast Oklahoma, and southern Arkansas into western and southern Louisiana.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Within an increasingly amplified large-scale pattern, a trough centered over the central and southern High Plains this morning will continue to amplify and dig southeastward toward the Ozarks and Ark-La-Tex region through tonight.

sections.title: Southeast OK/east TX and LA/AR/MS
sections.text: An increasingly moisture-rich warm-sector boundary layer will continue to develop northward across much of east/central TX and LA, with near 70F surface dewpoints becoming increasingly established across southeast TX and southern LA by early afternoon, with middle to upper 60s F surface dewpoints as far north as the Ark-La-Tex vicinity. This increasingly moist warm sector will be in place ahead of a cold front that will advance southeastward across southeast OK and much of central/east TX and Ark-La-Tex vicinity, and along a maritime-related warm front moving northward into and across southeast TX and southern LA. Multiple corridors of increasingly strong thunderstorms are likely this morning. One area is across southeast TX/upper TX coast vicinity into southern LA. A very moist low-level air mass (near 70F to lower 70s F surface dewpoints) continues to approach the coast early today. Additional moistening/ascent early today will allow convection to continue to increase and mature with an intensification of surface-based thunderstorms this morning into afternoon. outlooks.summary: A swath of severe storms is expected through tonight, most likely across east Texas and Louisiana. A few tornadoes, damaging winds, and large hail will be possible.

sections.title: Gulf Coast States
sections.text: Main change this outlook is to reduce probabilities over parts of the Mid/Deep South where surface-based buoyancy will be substantially limited owing to a large MCS ongoing across LA and southeast TX. This MCS will likely persist amid continued low-level warm air advection atop an established cold pool. Given the overlap of high-quality boundary-layer moisture characterized by middle 70s surface dew points with the eastern periphery of very steep mid-level lapse rates of 8.5-9.5 degree C/km between 700-500 mb, setup will favor robust, regenerative updrafts across the west/east-oriented convective outflow. All hazards will remain possible. Farther northwest, storm development will increase this afternoon as MLCIN weakens along a southeast-moving cold front in east TX. Given the undercutting nature of the front and veered low-level flow, storms should quickly grow upscale into clusters/lines. Amid moderate to strong buoyancy and strengthening mid-level west-southwest winds, setup should support bowing line segments and embedded supercell structures with all hazards possible. outlooks.summary: A severe threat will continue across east Texas, Louisiana into southern Mississippi through tonight. Damaging winds, isolated large hail and a tornado threat will be possible. Several changes have been made to the outlook for this issuance. The first change is to remove the enhanced risk area across Louisiana where the airmass has been worked over. Severe storms are ongoing to the southeast of Dallas and these storms should continue east-southeastward across the remainder of east Texas this afternoon. A wind damage threat associated with these storms appears to be enough to keep the enhanced risk area from near Tyler, Texas southeastward across the Lufkin vicinity to near the Sabine River. The second change is to remove the slight risk area from southwestern Arkansas where the airmass has also been worked over by an area of rain. The slight risk has also be trimmed southward across northeast Louisiana and south-central Mississippi. The third change is to remove the marginal risk area from central Arkansas where the atmosphere is relatively stable. mesoscale_discussions.summary: WW issuance is likely within the hour. Storms will continue to increase in intensity (as observed with ongoing activity north of HOU and across southwest LA at 12Z) and coverage this morning.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A couple of storms have developed and intensified across southeast TX (near and north of the Houston metro), and moving onshore the southwest LA coastal region from the northwest Gulf of Mexico per trends in mosaic radar imagery. Although overall storm coverage is limited at this time, observational data indicated the storms that have formed have developed strong updrafts (some with weak low- to mid-level rotation and rapidly cooling cloud tops to 50,000+ ft.). Early morning surface analyses showed a warm front advancing north across southeast TX and approaching the LA coast with storms thus far developing near this front. Rich low-level moisture was located across the warm sector (dew points into the lower 70s). This combined with the presence of steep midlevel lapse rates (exceeding 8 C/km) per objective analyses and 12Z soundings will continue to contribute to a destabilizing air mass from south to north and MLCAPE ranging from 1500-2500 J/kg this morning. Meanwhile, water-vapor imagery showed an eastward-moving midlevel shortwave trough in south-central to southeast TX as 700-mb winds have veered to westerly at SJT/DRT and EWX with the passage of this trough. Forcing for ascent with this trough and within the exit region of an accompanying 50-55 kt westerly 500-mb jet will support further thunderstorm development this morning across southeast TX into southwest LA. The favorable thermodynamics and strong low-level (increasing SRH values) and deep-layer shear (vertically veering winds) will favor organized storms, with hail as the initial threat. However, the ongoing reduction of inhibition will allow for storms to become surface based this morning with additional severe-weather hazards (including damaging winds and a tornado threat).

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WW issuance is possible this morning as storms continue to develop across southeast OK toward the Ark-La-Tex region. Hail should be the initial severe hazard, though damaging winds will be possible as well.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in mosaic radar imagery indicated new thunderstorm development across southeast OK since 1130Z, in vicinity of what appears to be a triple point or surface low located near KMLC. An increase in deep-layer forcing for ascent is expected across the discussion area, given the approach of a digging/amplifying shortwave trough into the southern Plains and ongoing low-level warm air advection. This forcing for ascent will continue to spread across the northern extent of moisture return/destabilization further supporting additional storm development. This scenario is favored by several CAMs which suggest initial development may tend to struggle to sustain updrafts. This is likely due to weak bulk shear across this region at this time, though effective bulk shear will increase as vertically veering winds strengthen today supporting greater updraft sustenance and storm organization. Steep midlevel lapse rates (8-9.5 C/km) per 12Z area soundings will favor hail as the initial threat as has been observed per MRMS MESH data, thus far. Otherwise, damaging winds and some tornado threat will be possible as storms eventually become surface based.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for isolated tornadoes will persist mainly over the southern half of WW 190 from southeast TX into southern LA. Otherwise storms will also remain capable of producing large hail over the remainder of the WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Late this morning a quasi-stationary front extends through southern LA into southeast TX, and numerous storms including supercells are developing along and north of this boundary. The warm sector is moderately unstable south of the front with upper 60s to low 70s F surface dewpoints and steep mid-level lapse rates supporting 1500-2500 J/kg MLCAPE, but with more limited instability in cool sector. A 40 kt southwesterly low-level jet will migrate through southeast TX into the lower MS valley through the afternoon in association with a shortwave trough advancing through the southern plains. The low-level jet should promote persistent development of storms along the southern and southwestern flank of the evolving MCS and the stronger storms should remain confined to along and just south of the warm front where inflow of high theta-e air will be unimpeded. The Lake Charles VWP has shown an increase in low-level hodograph size during the last hour with vertical wind profiles supportive of supercells with low-level mesocyclones along with an attendant tornado threat with any surface based supercell structures. Farther north into central LA tendency will probably be for storms to continue to weaken as they move atop a more stable boundary layer, but the the stronger storms may remain capable of producing mainly large hail. ..Dial.. 05/03/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for severe storms including mainly damaging wind and large hail, but with a couple tornadoes possible is expected to increase through the afternoon from portions of north central, central and northeast Texas.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms are beginning to increase along a cold front that extends from southeast OK through north central TX. This boundary is preceded by an outflow boundary/gravity wave, that extends from northeast through central TX. The warm sector is moderately unstable with steep mid-level lapse rates present, but an inversion due to warm air at base of an elevated mixed layer still exists over much of this region. WV imagery implies forcing for ascent associated with a southeastward-advancing shortwave trough is beginning to overtake the front. This corridor of deeper ascent should help to weaken the inversion layer with time, and storms should gradually intensify along the cold front. Vertical wind profiles/shear remains weak, but some strengthening is expected as at mid-level jet within the base of the trough overspreads the warm sector. Both multicell and supercell modes are expected this afternoon with primary threats being damaging wind and large hail. A limiting factor for a more robust tornado threat is the veered low-level winds which will limit 0-1 km hodograph size, except closer to the low-level jet axis over northeast TX.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for damaging winds, severe hail, and a tornado or two will continue through the early afternoon, especially south and east of I-30.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms continue to increase in coverage and intensity along a cold front pushing south and east through north central Texas. The surface to mid-level vertical bulk wind shear has remained in the 25-30 kt range, which has prevented more organized supercell structures from developing thus far. However, rapidly strengthening low-to-mid-level wind fields will push the deep-layer bulk wind shear into the 40-50 kt range in the next few hours. Combined with surface temperatures warming into the upper 70s to mid 80s, a very moist boundary layer, and very steep mid-level lapse rates, this rapid uptick in shear is expected to contribute to a rapid increase in storm organization including line segments and supercells. Storm coverage also is expected to increase rapidly in this time given the strong mid-level forcing for ascent spreading over the region during peak heating. Recent high-resolution guidance suggests storms will develop ahead of the cold front over northeast Texas. Despite the stronger mid-level flow overspreading this area, the threat for a tornado or two is limited by a trend for veering low-level winds in the heated air mass ahead of the cold front. Backed low-level winds, as seen in recent KSHV VAD wind profiles and the 18z raob, appear to be limited to the areas that remain in the relatively cool convective outflow in which temperatures remain in the upper 60s to low 70s. Another limiting factor for a more robust tornado (and possibly the severe wind threat in the next few hours) is somewhat modest 0-3 km lapse rates related to the relatively warm EML base, despite the strong surface heating. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Overall severe threat across most of the remainder of WW 190 has transitioned to isolated hail and a few strong to damaging wind gusts. An isolated tornado or two remains possible, mainly from from the extreme southeast TX coast and east along the LA coast.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early this afternoon a convective outflow boundary extends from the LA coast northwest into southeast TX. This boundary is intersecting a southeast-moving gravity wave over southeast TX where new storms are developing. South of the outflow boundary, winds have veered to southwesterly over the southeast TX warm sector, which is limiting low-level hodograph size. Storms initiating within zone of enhanced ascent along boundary intersection near and west of Lufkin TX may intensify as they develop southeast through the strongly unstable warm sector. Here, unidirectional wind profiles and vertical shear will strengthen with time supporting potential for organized severe storms capable of mainly damaging wind and large hail. Otherwise most storms have become slightly elevated over southern and central LA to the north of the outflow boundary where primary threat has transitioned to isolated hail and damaging wind. A tornado or two remains possible mainly with any storm that can develop along the modifying outflow boundary over coastal southeast TX and LA. ..Dial.. 05/03/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Tornado watch 190 will likely need to be replaced by another WW before expiration time of 22Z. Isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts will be the main threats though a couple of tornadoes cannot be ruled out.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms continue developing along a southeast-advancing cold front across a portion central through northeast TX as well as north of a large convective outflow boundary across southern LA. Atmosphere is moderately to strongly unstable over southeast TX, and storms will likely continue developing along the cold front/outflow boundary intersection and some distance south along the cold front into southeast TX this evening. Southward extent of development will be limited by a stronger cap and tendency for deeper forcing associated with the shortwave trough to remain north of warm sector. Deep-layer winds and effective bulk shear have increased and are sufficient for organized structures including supercells, but low-level hodograph size is limited in warm sector. Primary threats should be large hail and damaging wind, but a conditional risk for a couple of tornadoes will exist with storms interacting with modifying outflow boundary. ..Dial.. 05/03/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for damaging wind gusts and severe hail continues for ww191, especially south of I-20.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms continue to organize along and ahead of a cold front amidst strengthening low-to-mid level westerly winds/deep-layer shear. North and east of I-20, only a narrow corridor of significant instability remains sandwiched between the cold front to the west and reinforced convective outflow to the east. Furthermore the spreading of anvil clouds/precipitation from the upstream storms will likely limit the severe potential in this area. South of the latitude of Longview/Tyler the warm sector widens considerably with MLCAPE values now in the 2500-3500 J/kg range. The limiting factors for a more robust severe/tornado potential in the remaining watch area continues to be the relatively modest low-level lapse rates and veered low-level winds in the significantly unstable air. This trend should continue as the storms move through the eastern portions of the watch in the next hour or two. A convective mode of line segments/clusters with some supercell structures is expected to continue with some potential increase in organization as the main mid-level jet overspreads the area. These cells continue to pose a risk for damaging wind gusts and severe hail.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Marginal wind/hail risk may persist for another couple of hours on cold side of outflow, but a watch is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Bands of elevated thunderstorms are ongoing over south central LA, in a zone of pronounced low-level warm advection atop the cold pool generated by numerous thunderstorms through the day. Surface observations show temperatures and dewpoints in the mid-low 60s, with the buoyancy feeding the storms rooted above the stable surface layer. Strong storm-relative inflow from the southeast in the low levels, along the northeast edge of the steeper midlevel lapse rates, should help maintain the forward-propagating storms, as well as a marginal risk for strong wind gusts and some hail. However, the threat for damaging winds will be largely mitigated by the stable near-surface layer within the cold pool. Thus, an additional watch is not currently anticipated across southern LA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/severe thunderstorms will spread across the southeast half of WW192 over the next several hours. Locally damaging winds and isolated large hail remain possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection has gradually increased along a cold front as it surges south into the Coastal Plain of TX...arcing west to near the southern end of the escarpment. This frontal convection appears to be partly influenced by a narrow band of steep low-level lapse rates which extends ahead of the front from the higher Mexican terrain into the western flank of an extensive MCS. This eastern complex of storms is propagating toward the lower Sabine River Valley which has experienced extensive convective overturning from earlier storms. However, a reservoir of moderate-high instability currently resides across south-central TX where SBCAPE values are on the order of 4000 J/kg. 00z soundings from CRP and DRT exhibit steep mid-level lapse rates, but notably capped along the middle TX Coast. It appears convection will continue to be concentrated near the front due to aforementioned capping and remain isolated west of WW192. Otherwise, frontal MCS should propagate across the remainder of the watch this evening with wind/hail possible. ..Darrow.. 05/04/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
